intro.title: Welcome to Sidi Ifni — Art Deco on the Atlantic
intro.p1: Sidi Ifni sits on Morocco's southern Atlantic coast, about two and a half hours south of Agadir via Tiznit. Until 1969 it was a Spanish enclave (Ifni). That past still shows in the white and blue Art Deco buildings, the former Plaza de España and a laid-back fishing-town rhythm rarely found on busier coastal strips.
intro.p2: The town itself is compact: walk the colonial centre, watch the port, then day-trip to Legzira's natural stone arches a short drive north. Ideal for one or two nights between Tiznit, Mirleft and the road toward Guelmim or the Anti-Atlas.

artdeco.title: Art Deco centre & Plaza
artdeco.p1: Sidi Ifni's centre still carries the geometry of the Spanish period: curved balconies, white walls, blue details and a main square long known as Plaza de España. Walk slowly — the charm is in the façades and the quiet scale, not in museums.
artdeco.p2: Morning light is soft on the white buildings; late afternoon warms the stone. Cafés around the square are natural pauses between short loops of the old streets.
artdeco.tip: Combine the centre walk with the port in the same half-day.

port.title: Fishing port
port.p1: The fishing port is the working edge of Sidi Ifni. Boats, nets and the day's catch set a different pace from the Art Deco streets above. It is a place to watch rather than a polished tourist stop.
port.p2: Late afternoon is lively when boats return. Respect the work areas and ask before photographing people closely.
port.tip: Good light near sunset; keep a respectful distance from active docks.

legzira.title: Legzira beach & arches
legzira.p1: Legzira, a short drive north of Sidi Ifni, is famous for its natural stone arches on the beach. Tide and light change the scene hour by hour — the classic postcard view is best checked against local tide timing.
legzira.p2: Reach it by grand taxi, shared transport or private car. Wear shoes you can walk on sand and wet rock; facilities are limited so bring water.
legzira.tip: Go for low-to-mid tide if you want to walk closer to the arches. Sunset is popular — arrive early.

beach.title: Sidi Ifni beach & corniche
beach.p1: Sidi Ifni's own beach stretches along the Atlantic with a simple corniche. It is less dramatic than Legzira but ideal for an evening walk without leaving town.
beach.p2: Swimming depends on swell and local advice — the Atlantic here can be strong. Sunsets over the water are the main daily show.
beach.tip: Sunset walk on the corniche after dinner in town.

church.title: Spanish church & civic buildings
church.p1: Several buildings from the Spanish period remain: the former church and civic structures that once served the enclave. They are part of the open-air story of Ifni rather than a single ticketed site.
church.p2: Access and condition can vary; treat them as heritage landmarks on a walking loop of the centre.
church.tip: Pair with the Plaza and Art Deco streets in one easy circuit.

mirleft.title: Mirleft (day trip)
mirleft.p1: Mirleft lies on the coast between Tiznit and Sidi Ifni. It has become a small surf and café stop with a more village feel than a large resort.
mirleft.p2: Easy as a half-day or a night if you want beach time between the silver city and Art Deco Sidi Ifni.
mirleft.tip: Combine with the road trip from Tiznit if you are driving south.

q1.question: How long should I stay in Sidi Ifni?
q1.answer: One night is enough for the centre and a Legzira visit; two nights if you want a slower pace and Mirleft or extra beach time.

q2.question: Is Legzira worth it from Sidi Ifni?
q2.answer: Yes — it is the main nature highlight of the area. Plan around tide and light if you care about photos of the arches.

q3.question: How do I get to Sidi Ifni?
q3.answer: Most visitors come by road from Agadir via Tiznit (about 2.5–3 hours). Grands taxis and buses serve the route; a rental car is flexible for Legzira and Mirleft.

q4.question: Is Sidi Ifni good for swimming?
q4.answer: The Atlantic can be rough. Prefer calm days, follow local advice, and treat Legzira mainly as a walk and photo stop rather than a swim beach.
